---
title: "The mathematics behind effectzones"
description: >
  Every calculation the package performs, worked through step by step
  with interactive examples.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE)
library(effectzones)

# --- helpers for the step-by-step calculators -------------------------------
esc <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("&", "&amp;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("<", "&lt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub(">", "&gt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  gsub("\"", "&quot;", x, fixed = TRUE)
}
# TeX, rendered with KaTeX in the browser
tx <- function(x, display = FALSE) {
  sprintf('<span class="ez-tex"%s data-tex="%s"><code>%s</code></span>',
          if (display) ' data-display="1"' else "", esc(x), esc(x))
}
# numbers: n(x) for display, digits significant
n <- function(x, digits = 4) {
  out <- formatC(signif(x, digits), format = "fg", digits = digits)
  out <- sub("\\.$", "", trimws(out))
  sub("^-", "\u2212", out)
}
nt <- function(x, digits = 4) sub("\u2212", "-", n(x, digits)) # for TeX
swatch <- function(col) {
  sprintf('<span class="ez-swatch" style="background:%s" title="%s"></span><code>%s</code>',
          col, col, col)
}
step <- function(text, math = NULL, note = NULL) {
  list(text = text, math = math, note = note)
}
stepper <- function(id, title, given, steps, code = NULL) {
  li <- vapply(seq_along(steps), function(i) {
    s <- steps[[i]]
    paste0(
      '<li class="ez-step">',
      '<div class="ez-text">', s$text, "</div>",
      if (!is.null(s$math)) paste0('<div class="ez-math">', tx(s$math, TRUE), "</div>"),
      if (!is.null(s$note)) paste0('<div class="ez-note">', s$note, "</div>"),
      "</li>"
    )
  }, character(1))
  html <- paste0(
    '<div class="ez-stepper" id="', id, '">',
    '<div class="ez-title">', title, "</div>",
    '<div class="ez-given"><span class="ez-given-label">Given</span> ', given, "</div>",
    '<ol class="ez-steps">', paste(li, collapse = ""), "</ol>",
    if (!is.null(code)) paste0('<div class="ez-code"><span class="ez-given-label">In R</span><pre><code>',
                               esc(code), "</code></pre></div>"),
    '<div class="ez-controls">',
    '<button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary ez-prev">&larr; Back</button>',
    '<span class="ez-count" aria-live="polite"></span>',
    '<button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-primary ez-next">Next step &rarr;</button>',
    '<button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-link ez-all">Show all</button>',
    '<button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-link ez-reset">Start over</button>',
    "</div>",
    '<div class="ez-progress"><div class="ez-bar"></div></div>',
    "</div>"
  )
  knitr::asis_output(paste0("\n```{=html}\n", html, "\n```\n"))
}
```

```{=html}
(function () {
  function renderTex(root) {
    var els = root.querySelectorAll(".ez-tex");
    for (var i = 0; i < els.length; i++) {
      try {
        window.katex.render(els[i].getAttribute("data-tex"), els[i], {
          displayMode: els[i].hasAttribute("data-display"), throwOnError: false
        });
      } catch (e) {}
    }
  }
  function withKatex(cb) {
    if (window.katex) return cb();
    var css = document.createElement("link");
    css.rel = "stylesheet";
    css.href = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.11/dist/katex.min.css";
    document.head.appendChild(css);
    var js = document.createElement("script");
    js.src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.16.11/dist/katex.min.js";
    js.onload = cb;
    document.head.appendChild(js);
  }
  function setup(box) {
    var steps = box.querySelectorAll(".ez-step");
    var n = steps.length, k = 1;
    var prev = box.querySelector(".ez-prev"), next = box.querySelector(".ez-next");
    var all = box.querySelector(".ez-all"), reset = box.querySelector(".ez-reset");
    var count = box.querySelector(".ez-count"), bar = box.querySelector(".ez-bar");
    var code = box.querySelector(".ez-code");
    function show() {
      for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        steps[i].classList.toggle("ez-hidden", i >= k);
        steps[i].classList.toggle("ez-current", i === k - 1);
      }
      count.textContent = "Step " + k + " of " + n;
      bar.style.width = (100 * k / n) + "%";
      prev.disabled = k <= 1;
      next.disabled = k >= n;
      next.textContent = k >= n ? "Done" : "Next step \u2192";
      if (code) code.style.display = k >= n ? "" : "none";
    }
    next.addEventListener("click", function () { if (k < n) { k++; show(); } });
    prev.addEventListener("click", function () { if (k > 1) { k--; show(); } });
    all.addEventListener("click", function () { k = n; show(); });
    reset.addEventListener("click", function () { k = 1; show(); });
    show();
  }
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
    var boxes = document.querySelectorAll(".ez-stepper");
    for (var i = 0; i < boxes.length; i++) setup(boxes[i]);
    withKatex(function () { renderTex(document); });
  });
})();
</script>
```

effectzones draws backgrounds; it never tests or classifies an estimate.
But drawing a background still involves arithmetic: converting
standardised thresholds to the scale of the data, choosing the right
standard deviation, translating effect sizes into odds ratios, placing soft
boundaries and fitting them into a panel. This article works through every
one of those calculations.

Each **calculator** below starts from a concrete example. Press **Next
step** to reveal one step at a time, **Back** to go back, or **Show all**.
The numbers are computed by R with effectzones itself when this page is
built, so they are exactly what the package uses.

## 1. The pooled within-group SD

Most effect-size benchmarks are standardised: a "medium" d of 0.5 means a
difference of half a standard deviation. To draw it behind contrasts in the
outcome's own units we need that SD. In a one-way ANOVA with $k$ groups the
residual standard deviation is the pooled within-group SD,

$$
s_p = \sqrt{\mathrm{MSE}}
    = \sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{k} (n_i - 1)\, s_i^2}{N - k}},
$$

the usual denominator of Cohen's $d$. It is the same quantity the ANOVA
$F$ test and the Tukey intervals rely on, under the same equal-variance
assumption, so `plot_contrasts()` takes it from a one-way model
automatically.

```{r pooled}
fit <- aov(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth)
g <- split(PlantGrowth$weight, PlantGrowth$group)
ni <- vapply(g, length, numeric(1))
si <- vapply(g, sd, numeric(1))
ss <- sum((ni - 1) * si^2)
N <- sum(ni); k <- length(ni); df <- N - k
mse <- ss / df
sp <- sqrt(mse)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(sp, pooled_sd(fit))))
tab <- paste0(
  "<table><tr><th>group</th><th>", tx("n_i"), "</th><th>", tx("s_i"), "</th></tr>",
  paste0("<tr><td>", names(ni), "</td><td>", ni, "</td><td>", n(si), "</td></tr>", collapse = ""),
  "</table>"
)
stepper("sd-pooled", "Pooled SD of the PlantGrowth one-way ANOVA",
  given = paste("plant dry weight in three groups (", tx("k = 3"), ")."),
  steps = list(
    step(paste("Start from the size and SD of each group:", tab)),
    step("Weight each group's variance by its degrees of freedom and add them up: the within-group sum of squares.",
         sprintf("\\textstyle\\sum (n_i - 1)s_i^2 = %s", paste(sprintf("%d \\times %s^2", ni - 1, nt(si)), collapse = " + ")),
         note = paste("= ", n(ss, 5))),
    step("Divide by the residual degrees of freedom to get the mean squared error.",
         sprintf("\\mathrm{MSE} = \\frac{%s}{N - k} = \\frac{%s}{%d - %d} = %s", nt(ss, 5), nt(ss, 5), N, k, nt(mse, 5))),
    step("Take the square root: this is the pooled within-group SD.",
         sprintf("s_p = \\sqrt{%s} = %s", nt(mse, 5), nt(sp, 4)),
         note = "It equals the residual SD of the fitted model, sigma(fit).")
  ),
  code = "fit <- aov(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth)\npooled_sd(fit)"
)
```

## 2. From standardised thresholds to boundaries on the data scale

A standardised cut-point $c$ becomes a pair of boundaries around the null,
$\text{null} \pm c \cdot \mathrm{SD}$. Effect sizes on the correlation,
$\eta^2$ or $f$ scale are drawn on their own scale only; there is no
conversion from them to raw differences.

```{r d-to-raw}
cuts <- es_benchmarks("cohen_d")$cuts
raw <- to_plot_scale(es_benchmarks("cohen_d"), sd = sp)$cuts
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(raw, cuts * sp)))
stepper("d-to-raw", "Cohen's d benchmarks behind the PlantGrowth contrasts",
  given = paste("cut-points", tx("d = 0.2,\\ 0.5,\\ 0.8"), "(Cohen 1988) and", tx(sprintf("s_p = %s", nt(sp))), "from calculator 1."),
  steps = list(
    step("Multiply each cut-point by the SD.",
         sprintf("%s", paste(sprintf("%s \\times %s = %s", cuts, nt(sp), nt(raw)), collapse = ",\\quad "))),
    step("Place a boundary on each side of the null (0 for a difference).",
         sprintf("\\pm %s,\\quad \\pm %s,\\quad \\pm %s", nt(raw[1]), nt(raw[2]), nt(raw[3]))),
    step(paste("Read off the zones (in kg of dry weight). A contrast whose interval lies between",
               n(-raw[1]), "and", n(raw[1]), "kg sits in the <em>negligible</em> zone; beyond",
               n(raw[3]), "kg in either direction it reaches the <em>large</em> zone."),
         sprintf("\\underbrace{|x| < %s}_{\\text{negligible}}\\;\\;\\underbrace{%s \\le |x| < %s}_{\\text{small}}\\;\\;\\underbrace{%s \\le |x| < %s}_{\\text{medium}}\\;\\;\\underbrace{|x| \\ge %s}_{\\text{large}}",
                 nt(raw[1]), nt(raw[1]), nt(raw[2]), nt(raw[2]), nt(raw[3]), nt(raw[3])))
  ),
  code = "to_plot_scale(es_benchmarks(\"cohen_d\"), sd = pooled_sd(fit))"
)
```

## 3. Which SD when the model has several terms

With more than one term the residual SD has the variance of *every other
term* removed. That is right for factors the experimenter manipulated
(their variation does not exist in the population) and too small for
factors that were only measured (sex, age, site, baseline covariates),
which are ordinary differences between people. The generalized
standardizer (Olejnik & Algina 2003) keeps measured variation in the SD:
refit the model with **only the manipulated factors** and use its residual
SD. Whether a factor was manipulated or measured is a fact about the
design, not the data, which is why `plot_contrasts()` asks instead of
guessing.

```{r co2}
co2 <- subset(CO2, conc == 1000)
fit_full <- aov(uptake ~ Treatment + Type, data = co2)
fit_manip <- update(fit_full, . ~ Treatment)
s_full <- pooled_sd(fit_full)
s_manip <- pooled_sd(fit_manip)
df_full <- fit_full$df.residual
df_manip <- fit_manip$df.residual
stepper("sd-generalized", "Chilling (manipulated) and plant origin (measured) in the CO2 data",
  given = paste("CO\u2082 uptake of 12 plants at the highest concentration;",
                "<code>Treatment</code> (chilled or not) was assigned, <code>Type</code> (Quebec or Mississippi) is the plants' origin."),
  steps = list(
    step("Fit the model with both terms. Its residual SD has the large difference between origins removed.",
         sprintf("s_{\\text{residual}} = \\sqrt{\\mathrm{MSE}_{\\text{Treatment + Type}}} = %s \\quad (%d\\ \\text{df})", nt(s_full), df_full)),
    step("Refit with the manipulated factor only. Origin is ordinary variation between plants, so it goes back into the error term.",
         sprintf("s_{\\text{gen}} = \\sqrt{\\mathrm{MSE}_{\\text{Treatment}}} = %s \\quad (%d\\ \\text{df})", nt(s_manip), df_manip)),
    step("Compare. Using the residual SD would shrink every zone by this factor.",
         sprintf("\\frac{s_{\\text{gen}}}{s_{\\text{residual}}} = \\frac{%s}{%s} = %s", nt(s_manip), nt(s_full), nt(s_manip / s_full, 3))),
    step("Translate a \"medium\" d = 0.5 into each scale.",
         sprintf("0.5 \\times %s = %s \\ \\mu\\text{mol/m}^2\\text{s} \\quad\\text{vs.}\\quad 0.5 \\times %s = %s", nt(s_full), nt(0.5 * s_full), nt(s_manip), nt(0.5 * s_manip)),
         note = "Only the second matches what \"half a standard deviation between plants\" means.")
  ),
  code = paste0(
    "fit <- aov(uptake ~ Treatment + Type, data = subset(CO2, conc == 1000))\n",
    "plot_contrasts(fit, which = \"Treatment\",\n",
    "  zones = geom_es_zones(es_benchmarks(\"cohen_d\"),\n",
    "                        sd = pooled_sd(update(fit, . ~ Treatment))))"
  )
)
```

The same logic applies to a randomised ANCOVA. Adjusting for a baseline
covariate with pooled within-group correlation $r$ removes a fraction $r^2$
of the outcome variance, so the adjusted residual SD relates to the
unadjusted within-group SD approximately as

$$
s_{\text{adj}} \approx s_{\text{unadj}} \sqrt{1 - r^2}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
s_{\text{unadj}} \approx \frac{s_{\text{adj}}}{\sqrt{1 - r^2}},
$$

(ignoring the one degree of freedom spent on the slope). The standardizer
for $d$ is $s_{\text{unadj}}$: the covariate improves precision, but people
still differ by that much.

## 4. The SD is an estimate too

The SD used to place the boundaries has sampling error. Under normality,
$(\nu\, s^2)/\sigma^2 \sim \chi^2_\nu$ with $\nu$ residual degrees of
freedom, which gives a confidence interval for $\sigma$:

$$
\left[\, s\sqrt{\frac{\nu}{\chi^2_{\nu,\,1-\alpha/2}}},\;
        s\sqrt{\frac{\nu}{\chi^2_{\nu,\,\alpha/2}}} \,\right].
$$

Each boundary $d \cdot s$ inherits that interval. effectzones does not yet
draw this uncertainty, so report it alongside the plot.

```{r sd-ci}
lo_q <- qchisq(0.975, df); hi_q <- qchisq(0.025, df)
s_lo <- sp * sqrt(df / lo_q); s_hi <- sp * sqrt(df / hi_q)
stepper("sd-ci", "95% confidence interval for the PlantGrowth SD",
  given = paste(tx(sprintf("s_p = %s", nt(sp))), "with", tx(sprintf("\\nu = %d", df)), "residual degrees of freedom (calculator 1)."),
  steps = list(
    step("Look up the chi-square quantiles that cut off 2.5% in each tail.",
         sprintf("\\chi^2_{%d,\\,0.975} = %s, \\qquad \\chi^2_{%d,\\,0.025} = %s", df, nt(lo_q), df, nt(hi_q))),
    step("Lower limit: divide by the larger quantile.",
         sprintf("%s \\sqrt{\\tfrac{%d}{%s}} = %s", nt(sp), df, nt(lo_q), nt(s_lo))),
    step("Upper limit: divide by the smaller quantile.",
         sprintf("%s \\sqrt{\\tfrac{%d}{%s}} = %s", nt(sp), df, nt(hi_q), nt(s_hi))),
    step("Carry it to a boundary. The \"medium\" boundary 0.5 SD could plausibly lie anywhere in",
         sprintf("0.5 \\times [%s,\\ %s] = [%s,\\ %s]\\ \\text{kg}", nt(s_lo), nt(s_hi), nt(0.5 * s_lo), nt(0.5 * s_hi)),
         note = sprintf("A point boundary at %s kg hides that spread.", n(0.5 * sp)))
  ),
  code = paste0(
    "s <- pooled_sd(fit); nu <- fit$df.residual\n",
    "s * sqrt(nu / qchisq(c(0.975, 0.025), nu))"
  )
)
```

## 5. Soft boundaries

Benchmarks are conventions, not natural discontinuities, so by default
`geom_es_zones()` fades from one zone into the next. For a boundary at
distance $c$ from the null, with `softness` $= \lambda$ (default 0.1), the
transition spans

$$
\left[\, c - \tfrac{\lambda c}{2},\; c + \tfrac{\lambda c}{2} \,\right],
$$

drawn as $n$ thin rectangles (`n_slices`, default 40). Slice $j$ is
coloured at the fraction $t_j = (j - \tfrac12)/n$ of the way between the
two zone colours, interpolated in the perceptually uniform CIELAB space. If
two neighbouring transitions would overlap they are both cut back to the
midpoint between their boundaries. For ratio zones the same arithmetic is
done on the log scale.

```{r soft}
spec <- effectzones:::es_zone_spec(
  to_plot_scale(es_benchmarks("cohen_d"), sd = sp), null = 0,
  softness = 0.1, palette = "grey"
)
b <- spec$boundaries[spec$boundaries$at > 0, ][2, ] # the "medium" boundary
z_from <- spec$zones$colour[spec$zones$label == "small"][1]
z_to <- spec$zones$colour[spec$zones$label == "medium"][1]
nsl <- 40
tj <- (c(1, 20, 40) - 0.5) / nsl
cols <- scales::colour_ramp(c(z_from, z_to))(tj)
seg <- effectzones:::zone_segments(spec, n_slices = nsl)
stopifnot(all(cols %in% seg$fill))
stepper("soft", "The soft boundary between \"small\" and \"medium\" (PlantGrowth, d = 0.5)",
  given = paste(tx(sprintf("c = 0.5 \\times %s = %s", nt(sp), nt(b$at))), "kg,", tx("\\lambda = 0.1"), ",", tx("n = 40"), "slices, grey palette."),
  steps = list(
    step("Width of the transition: a tenth of the threshold.",
         sprintf("\\lambda c = 0.1 \\times %s = %s", nt(b$at), nt(0.1 * b$at))),
    step("Centre it on the threshold.",
         sprintf("[\\,%s - %s,\\; %s + %s\\,] = [\\,%s,\\; %s\\,]", nt(b$at), nt(0.05 * b$at), nt(b$at), nt(0.05 * b$at), nt(b$lo), nt(b$hi))),
    step("Cut it into 40 slices and give each one a mixing fraction, e.g. slices 1, 20 and 40:",
         sprintf("t_1 = \\tfrac{0.5}{40} = %s,\\quad t_{20} = \\tfrac{19.5}{40} = %s,\\quad t_{40} = \\tfrac{39.5}{40} = %s", nt(tj[1]), nt(tj[2]), nt(tj[3]))),
    step(paste0("Mix the two zone colours (", swatch(z_from), " small, ", swatch(z_to),
                " medium) at those fractions in CIELAB:", "<br>",
                "slice 1", swatch(cols[1]), " &nbsp; slice 20", swatch(cols[2]), " &nbsp; slice 40", swatch(cols[3])),
         note = "Each slice is then drawn with the layer's alpha (0.35 by default), so the gridlines and estimates stay visible.")
  ),
  code = "geom_es_zones(es_benchmarks(\"cohen_d\"), sd = pooled_sd(fit),\n              softness = 0.1, n_slices = 40)"
)
```

## 6. Ratios: zones on the log scale

Odds ratios and risk ratios are multiplicative, so their zones are placed
around $1$ on the log scale. A magnitude $c$ gives boundaries $1/c$ and $c$
(symmetric in $\log$), unless the thresholds specify a different magnitude
below the null (`cuts_lower`). On a `scale_x_log10()` axis, ggplot2 works
in $\log_{10}$ units, and the boundaries are transformed the same way as the
data.

```{r ratio}
c1 <- 1.68
stepper("ratio", "Placing the first Chen et al. odds-ratio boundary on a log axis",
  given = paste(tx("c = 1.68"), "(the \"small\" odds ratio at a 1% baseline risk), null", tx("= 1"), ", axis", tx("\\log_{10}"), "."),
  steps = list(
    step("Above the null: multiply.", sprintf("1 \\times %s = %s", c1, c1)),
    step("Below the null (symmetric case): divide.", sprintf("1 / %s = %s", c1, nt(1 / c1))),
    step("On the log scale the two are mirror images of each other.",
         sprintf("\\log(%s) = %s, \\qquad \\log(%s) = %s", c1, nt(log(c1)), nt(1 / c1), nt(log(1 / c1)))),
    step("ggplot2 places them at their log10 positions, exactly like the data.",
         sprintf("\\log_{10}(%s) = %s, \\qquad \\log_{10}(%s) = %s", nt(1 / c1), nt(log10(1 / c1)), c1, nt(log10(c1))),
         note = "Section 8 shows why, under Chen et al.'s own model, the lower boundary is not exactly 1/c.")
  ),
  code = "geom_es_zones(es_thresholds(c(1.68, 3.47, 6.71), c(\"negligible\", \"small\", \"medium\", \"large\"),\n                            metric = \"or\"), scale = \"log\", null = 1) +\n  scale_x_log10()"
)
```

## 7. From d to an odds ratio: Chinn's approximation

If a binary outcome arises from dichotomising a latent variable with a
logistic distribution, a shift of $d$ standard deviations corresponds to

$$
\log(\mathrm{OR}) = d \cdot \frac{\pi}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 1.814\, d
$$

(Chinn 2000). This is what `to_plot_scale(…, scale = "log")` uses for $d$
thresholds. It does not depend on the baseline risk, which is exactly
where it differs from Chen et al.

```{r chinn}
dd <- 0.5
lor <- dd * pi / sqrt(3)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(exp(lor), to_plot_scale(es_benchmarks("cohen_d"), scale = "log")$cuts[2])))
stepper("chinn", "A \"medium\" d = 0.5 as an odds ratio (Chinn 2000)",
  given = tx("d = 0.5"),
  steps = list(
    step("The scale factor of the logistic distribution.", sprintf("\\pi/\\sqrt{3} = %s", nt(pi / sqrt(3), 5))),
    step("Multiply.", sprintf("\\log(\\mathrm{OR}) = 0.5 \\times %s = %s", nt(pi / sqrt(3), 5), nt(lor, 5))),
    step("Exponentiate.", sprintf("\\mathrm{OR} = e^{%s} = %s", nt(lor, 5), nt(exp(lor))),
         note = "Compare Chen et al. at a 1% baseline: 3.47 (next section).")
  ),
  code = "to_plot_scale(es_benchmarks(\"cohen_d\"), scale = \"log\")$cuts"
)
```

## 8. From d to an odds ratio at a given baseline risk: Chen et al.

Chen, Cohen & Chen (2010) place both groups on a latent normal scale. With
event risk $p_0$ in the reference group, a shift $d$ gives the exposed
group's risk and the odds ratio

$$
p_1 = \Phi\!\left(\Phi^{-1}(p_0) + d\right), \qquad
\mathrm{OR} = \frac{p_1/(1-p_1)}{p_0/(1-p_0)} .
$$

This reproduces their published values (1.68, 3.47 and 6.71 at $p_0 = 1\%$;
1.52, 2.74 and 4.72 at $5\%$). Applied to a protective shift $-d$ it does
**not** give $1/\mathrm{OR}$, except at $p_0 = 0.5$, so effectzones
computes the boundaries below 1 from $-d$ directly.

```{r chen}
p0 <- 0.01; d8 <- 0.8
z0 <- qnorm(p0); z1 <- z0 + d8; p1 <- pnorm(z1)
or_up <- (p1 / (1 - p1)) / (p0 / (1 - p0))
z1m <- z0 - d8; p1m <- pnorm(z1m)
or_dn <- (p1m / (1 - p1m)) / (p0 / (1 - p0))
thr <- chen_or_thresholds(p0)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(or_up, thr$cuts[3])), isTRUE(all.equal(1 / or_dn, thr$cuts_lower[3])))
stepper("chen", "The \"large\" boundaries (d = \u00b10.8) at a 1% baseline risk",
  given = paste(tx("p_0 = 0.01"), "in the reference group,", tx("d = 0.8"), "."),
  steps = list(
    step("Move the baseline risk to the latent normal scale.",
         sprintf("z_0 = \\Phi^{-1}(0.01) = %s", nt(z0, 5))),
    step("Harmful direction: shift by +d and return to a risk.",
         sprintf("p_1 = \\Phi(%s + 0.8) = \\Phi(%s) = %s", nt(z0, 5), nt(z1, 5), nt(p1, 4))),
    step("Odds ratio for the harmful direction (the published value, 6.71).",
         sprintf("\\mathrm{OR} = \\frac{%s/(1-%s)}{0.01/0.99} = %s", nt(p1, 4), nt(p1, 4), nt(or_up, 4))),
    step("Protective direction: shift by \u2212d instead.",
         sprintf("p_1 = \\Phi(%s - 0.8) = \\Phi(%s) = %s", nt(z0, 5), nt(z1m, 5), nt(p1m, 4))),
    step("Odds ratio for the protective direction.",
         sprintf("\\mathrm{OR} = \\frac{%s/(1-%s)}{0.01/0.99} = %s = 1/%s", nt(p1m, 4), nt(p1m, 4), nt(or_dn, 4), nt(1 / or_dn, 4)),
         note = sprintf("Mirroring would have put this boundary at 1/%s = %s, so the protective \"large\" zone would start too close to 1.", n(or_up), n(1 / or_up)))
  ),
  code = "chen_or_thresholds(0.01)   # any baseline risk: chen_or_thresholds(0.2)"
)
```

## 9. Distribution-based (provisional) MCIDs

A distribution-based MCID describes the spread or the measurement error of
a score, not what patients consider worthwhile, so effectzones marks it
provisional. Two rules are offered:

$$
\text{half SD} = 0.5\, s, \qquad
\text{SEM} = s\sqrt{1 - r_{xx}},
$$

where $r_{xx}$ is the instrument's reliability (Norman, Sloan & Wyrwich
2003; Wyrwich, Tierney & Wolinsky 1999). Half an SD is exactly Cohen's
"medium" $d = 0.5$, which is why a distribution-based MCID adds no clinical
information beyond the effect-size zones.

```{r mcid-dist}
sem <- mcid_distribution(sd = 10, method = "sem", reliability = 0.84)
half <- mcid_distribution(sd = 10)
stepper("mcid-dist", "Half-SD and SEM for a score with SD 10 and reliability 0.84",
  given = paste(tx("s = 10"), ",", tx("r_{xx} = 0.84"), "."),
  steps = list(
    step("Half an SD.", sprintf("0.5 \\times 10 = %s", nt(half$upper))),
    step("The unreliable fraction of the variance.", "1 - 0.84 = 0.16"),
    step("One standard error of measurement.", sprintf("10 \\times \\sqrt{0.16} = 10 \\times 0.4 = %s", nt(sem$upper))),
    step("Either value becomes a symmetric, provisional MCID.",
         sprintf("\\text{harm} < %s \\le \\text{trivial} \\le %s < \\text{benefit}", nt(-sem$upper), nt(sem$upper)),
         note = "The legend then reads \"MCID (provisional, distribution-based)\".")
  ),
  code = "mcid_distribution(sd = 10, method = \"sem\", reliability = 0.84)"
)
```

## 10. MCID zones: asymmetry, direction, ranges and multiples

An MCID defines a trivial zone $[\ell, u]$ around the null, with $\ell < 0 < u$
allowed to differ in size. Which side is benefit depends on `direction`. A
range for either threshold (an uncertain MCID) is drawn as a fade across
the range, using the same slicing as section 5. With
`beyond = "multiples"`, extra boundaries at $2\ell, 3\ell$ and $2u, 3u$
deepen the colour; this requires point thresholds, because multiples of an
uncertain MCID would be uncertain too.

```{r mcid-zones}
m_pt <- mcid_thresholds(lower = -0.25, upper = 0.3)
spec_m <- effectzones:::mcid_zone_spec(m_pt, null = 0, softness = NULL,
                                       beyond = "multiples", palette = "diverging")
brk <- effectzones:::zone_breaks(spec_m)
m_rg <- mcid_thresholds(lower = -0.25, upper = c(0.3, 0.5))
stepper("mcid-zones", "Zones for an asymmetric MCID (\u22120.25 / +0.3, higher is better)",
  given = paste(tx("\\ell = -0.25"), ",", tx("u = 0.3"), ", <code>direction = \"higher_better\"</code>."),
  steps = list(
    step("Three zones, with hard edges at the thresholds.",
         "\\underbrace{x < -0.25}_{\\text{harm}} \\quad \\underbrace{-0.25 \\le x \\le 0.3}_{\\text{trivial}} \\quad \\underbrace{x > 0.3}_{\\text{benefit}}"),
    step("If lower values were better (<code>direction = \"lower_better\"</code>), the same boundaries would label the sides the other way round.",
         "\\underbrace{x < -0.25}_{\\text{benefit}} \\quad \\underbrace{-0.25 \\le x \\le 0.3}_{\\text{trivial}} \\quad \\underbrace{x > 0.3}_{\\text{harm}}"),
    step("With <code>beyond = \"multiples\"</code>, add boundaries at 2 and 3 times each threshold.",
         sprintf("%s", paste(nt(brk), collapse = ",\\ "))),
    step("If the improvement threshold were uncertain, say between 0.3 and 0.5, the trivial zone fades into benefit across that range instead of switching at one point.",
         "0.3 \\le x \\le 0.5:\\ \\text{trivial} \\rightarrow \\text{benefit}",
         note = "Multiples are then refused: \"2\u00d7\" could be anywhere from 0.6 to 1.0.")
  ),
  code = "geom_mcid_zones(mcid_thresholds(lower = -0.25, upper = 0.3), beyond = \"multiples\")\ngeom_mcid_zones(mcid_thresholds(lower = -0.25, upper = c(0.3, 0.5)))"
)
```

## 11. Where the intervals come from: Tukey's HSD

effectzones does not compute intervals; `plot_contrasts()` draws the ones
your analysis produced. For Tukey post-hoc comparisons (computed by
`stats::TukeyHSD()`), the family-wise interval for groups $i$ and $j$ is

$$
(\bar y_i - \bar y_j) \pm
\frac{q_{1-\alpha;\,k,\,\nu}}{\sqrt 2}
\sqrt{\mathrm{MSE}\left(\frac{1}{n_i} + \frac{1}{n_j}\right)},
$$

where $q$ is a quantile of the studentized range distribution.

```{r tukey}
tk <- TukeyHSD(fit)$group
mi <- vapply(g, mean, numeric(1))
dif <- mi["trt2"] - mi["trt1"]
q <- qtukey(0.95, k, df)
half_w <- q / sqrt(2) * sqrt(mse * (1 / ni["trt2"] + 1 / ni["trt1"]))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(dif - half_w), unname(tk["trt2-trt1", "lwr"]))))
stepper("tukey", "The trt2 \u2212 trt1 interval in PlantGrowth",
  given = paste(tx(sprintf("\\bar y_{\\text{trt2}} = %s,\\ \\bar y_{\\text{trt1}} = %s", nt(mi["trt2"]), nt(mi["trt1"]))), ",",
                tx("n = 10"), "per group,", tx(sprintf("\\mathrm{MSE} = %s", nt(mse))), ",", tx(sprintf("k = 3,\\ \\nu = %d", df)), "."),
  steps = list(
    step("Difference in means.", sprintf("%s - %s = %s", nt(mi["trt2"]), nt(mi["trt1"]), nt(dif))),
    step("Studentized range quantile for 95% family-wise coverage.", sprintf("q_{0.95;\\,3,\\,%d} = %s", df, nt(q))),
    step("Half-width of the interval.",
         sprintf("\\frac{%s}{\\sqrt 2}\\sqrt{%s\\left(\\tfrac{1}{10} + \\tfrac{1}{10}\\right)} = %s", nt(q), nt(mse), nt(half_w))),
    step("The interval drawn by <code>plot_contrasts()</code>, identical to <code>TukeyHSD()</code>.",
         sprintf("%s \\pm %s = [\\,%s,\\ %s\\,]", nt(dif), nt(half_w), nt(dif - half_w), nt(dif + half_w)),
         note = sprintf("Against the d zones of calculator 2 (boundaries at \u00b1%s, \u00b1%s, \u00b1%s kg), this interval runs from the small zone into the large zone.", n(raw[1]), n(raw[2]), n(raw[3])))
  ),
  code = "plot_contrasts(fit, zones = geom_es_zones(es_benchmarks(\"cohen_d\")))"
)
```

## 12. Fitting zones into the panel

Zone boundaries are layer parameters, not data, so by default they never
change the axis limits. The layer works out what is visible in three steps:
transform the boundaries like the data, keep the zones that reach the
visible range, and clip them to the panel. The visible range is the data
range expanded by ggplot2's default 5% on each side. (Zooming with
`coord_cartesian()` is applied only at drawing time, so the legend can
still list a zone that the zoom cuts away.)

```{r panel}
est <- c(tk[, "lwr"], tk[, "upr"])
rng <- range(est)
vis <- rng + c(-1, 1) * 0.05 * diff(rng)
zl <- c(-Inf, -raw[3], -raw[2], -raw[1], raw[1], raw[2], raw[3])
zh <- c(-raw[3], -raw[2], -raw[1], raw[1], raw[2], raw[3], Inf)
lab <- c("large", "medium", "small", "negligible", "small", "medium", "large")
keep <- zh > vis[1] & zl < vis[2]
raw3 <- es_benchmarks("cohen_d")$cuts * 3
zl3 <- c(-Inf, -raw3[3], -raw3[2], -raw3[1], raw3[1], raw3[2], raw3[3])
zh3 <- c(-raw3[3], -raw3[2], -raw3[1], raw3[1], raw3[2], raw3[3], Inf)
keep3 <- zh3 > vis[1] & zl3 < vis[2]
# the same rule as the package: check against the legend of the built plot
p3 <- plot_contrasts(fit, zones = geom_es_zones(es_benchmarks("cohen_d"), sd = 3, softness = 0))
lim3 <- ggplot2::ggplot_build(p3)$plot$scales$get_scales("es_zone")$get_limits()
stopifnot(identical(lim3, intersect(c("negligible", "small", "medium", "large"), lab[keep3])))
stepper("panel", "Which Cohen's d zones appear in the PlantGrowth Tukey plot",
  given = "the three Tukey intervals and the boundaries from calculator 2.",
  steps = list(
    step("The data span the lowest and highest interval limits.",
         sprintf("[\\,%s,\\ %s\\,]", nt(rng[1]), nt(rng[2]))),
    step("Expand by 5% of the width on each side to get the visible range.",
         sprintf("[\\,%s - %s,\\ %s + %s\\,] = [\\,%s,\\ %s\\,]", nt(rng[1]), nt(0.05 * diff(rng)), nt(rng[2]), nt(0.05 * diff(rng)), nt(vis[1]), nt(vis[2]))),
    step("Keep a zone if it overlaps the visible range: its upper end is above the left edge and its lower end below the right edge.",
         "\\text{keep} \\iff \\text{hi} > \\text{left} \\ \\text{and}\\ \\text{lo} < \\text{right}"),
    step(paste0("Result: ", paste(sprintf("%s %s", ifelse(keep, "\u2714", "\u2718"), lab), collapse = ", "),
                ". Every zone reaches the visible range, so all four labels appear in the legend; the outermost ones are clipped at the panel edges.")),
    step(paste0("Now suppose the benchmark's SD were 3 kg. The boundaries move to ",
                paste0("±", vapply(raw3, n, ""), collapse = ", "), " kg. ",
                "Result: ", paste(sprintf("%s %s", ifelse(keep3, "✔", "✘"), lab), collapse = ", "),
                ". The <em>large</em> zones begin beyond the visible range on both sides, so <em>large</em> is left out of the legend."))
  ),
  code = "plot_contrasts(fit, zones = geom_es_zones(es_benchmarks(\"cohen_d\"))) # expand = FALSE\nplot_contrasts(fit, zones = geom_es_zones(es_benchmarks(\"cohen_d\"), expand = TRUE))"
)
```

With `expand = TRUE` the finite boundaries are added to the scale's range
instead, so every cut-point is visible and every zone is listed.
